questions.question: What type of image is formed by a concave mirror when the object is placed at infinity?

options.text: Same size as the object and real

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Highly diminished, real and inverted**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When an object is placed at **infinity** in front of a concave mirror, the light rays from the object are considered to be parallel to the principal axis.
 
• These parallel rays converge at the **focus** of the concave mirror after reflection, forming the image.
 
• The image formed is **highly diminished** because all the rays meet at a single point, making the size of the image negligible compared to the object.
 
• The image is **real** because it is formed by the actual convergence of rays after reflection.
 
• The image is **inverted** because the reflected rays flip the orientation of the object.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concave Mirrors:**

 
 
• Concave mirrors are **spherical mirrors** that curve inward, resembling the inside of a sphere.
 
• They are capable of converging light rays and are commonly used in applications like telescopes, headlights, and shaving mirrors.
 
 
 
• **Image Formation Based on Object Position:**
 
 
• If the object is at infinity, the image is formed at the **focus**, is highly diminished, real, and inverted.
 
• If the object is beyond the center of curvature, the image is diminished, real, and inverted.
 
• If the object is at the center of curvature, the image is the same size, real, and inverted.
 
• If the object is between the focus and the mirror, the image is enlarged, virtual, and upright.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Concave Mirrors:**
 
 
• Used in **telescopes** for capturing distant celestial objects.
 
• Applied in **dentistry** and surgical procedures for magnified viewing.
 
• Used in **solar concentrators** to focus sunlight for energy generation.
 
• In car headlights, concave mirrors are used to create a parallel beam of light.
 
 
 
• **Real and Virtual Images:**
 
 
• A **real image** is formed when light rays actually converge, and it can be captured on a screen.
 
• A **virtual image** is formed when the rays appear to diverge from a point and cannot be captured on a screen.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Principal Focus:** The point where parallel rays converge after reflection in a concave mirror.
 
• **Center of Curvature:** The center of the sphere from which the mirror segment is derived.
 
• **Focal Length:** The distance between the principal focus and the pole of the mirror.
 
• **Mirror Formula:** The mathematical relationship governing mirrors: **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**, where f = focal length, v = image distance, and u = object distance.

questions.question: A common characteristic in all double displacement reaction is:

options.text: the reaction mixture is always colourless
exchange of metal ions between two metal salts
the reaction requires heat to initiate

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**exchange of metal ions between two metal salts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **double displacement reaction**, two ionic compounds exchange their ions to form two new compounds. This process involves the **exchange of cations (positively charged ions) and anions (negatively charged ions)** between the reacting substances.
 
• The general representation of a double displacement reaction is:

 **AB + CD → AD + CB**, where A and C are cations, and B and D are anions.
 
• This type of reaction typically occurs in aqueous solutions, where the ionic compounds are dissolved in water, allowing the ions to move freely and interact with each other.
 
• An example of a double displacement reaction is the reaction between **sodium chloride (NaCl)** and **silver nitrate (AgNO₃)**:

 **NaCl + AgNO₃ → NaNO₃ + AgCl (precipitate)**.
 
• Such reactions often result in the formation of a precipitate, a gas, or a neutral molecule such as water, making them easily observable in a laboratory setting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Characteristics of Double Displacement Reactions:**

 
 
• Double displacement reactions typically occur between two ionic compounds in aqueous solutions.
 
• These reactions often produce a **precipitate**, a gas, or a liquid (such as water) as a product.
 
• They do not involve the transfer of electrons, as opposed to redox reactions. Instead, they involve the **rearrangement of ions**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Double Displacement Reactions:**
 
 
• **Precipitation Reactions:** These occur when the exchange of ions results in the formation of an insoluble compound (precipitate). For example:

 **BaCl₂ + Na₂SO₄ → BaSO₄ (precipitate) + 2NaCl**.
 
• **Neutralization Reactions:** These occur between an acid and a base to produce water and a salt. For example:

 **HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O**.
 
• **Gas Formation Reactions:** In some cases, a gas is released as a result of the reaction. For example:

 **Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂ (gas)**.
 
 
 
• **Explanation of Incorrect Options:**
 
 
• **Option 1:** "Only one product is formed" – Incorrect. Double displacement reactions result in the formation of two products, not one.
 
• **Option 2:** "The reaction mixture is always colourless" – Incorrect. The reaction mixture can vary in colour based on the compounds involved and the products formed, such as precipitates of varying colours.
 
• **Option 4:** "The reaction requires heat to initiate" – Incorrect. Double displacement reactions usually occur spontaneously in aqueous solutions without the need for external heat.
 
 
 
• **Examples in Daily Life:**
 
 
• **Soap Scum Formation:** When soap reacts with hard water containing calcium or magnesium ions, a precipitate is formed.
 
• **Neutralization in Medicine:** Antacids neutralize stomach acid through double displacement reactions.

questions.question: Plastic waste has increased a lot in a city over the last 10 years. Which habit of people is most likely causing this?

options.text: More people are using buses and trains.
People are using more disposable items instead of long-lasting ones.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**People are using more disposable items instead of long-lasting ones**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plastic waste** has significantly increased due to the growing reliance on **disposable items** like single-use plastic bags, cutlery, bottles, and packaging. These items are often discarded after one use, contributing to the accumulation of non-biodegradable waste.
 
• Unlike **long-lasting or reusable items**, disposable items are designed for convenience and are frequently replaced, leading to higher consumption and waste generation. This habit is a primary driver of plastic pollution in cities.
 
• Disposable plastics are widely used in the **food and beverage industry**, e-commerce packaging, and retail sectors, which often prioritize cost-effectiveness and convenience over sustainability.
 
• While some cities have implemented **plastic bans** or promoted reusable alternatives, the persistent demand for disposable plastics undermines these efforts, further exacerbating the waste crisis.
 
• Increasing awareness about the environmental impact of disposable plastics and promoting behavioral changes, such as opting for **reusable alternatives**, can help reduce plastic waste significantly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Plastic waste statistics:**

 
 
• According to the **United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)**, over **300 million tons of plastic** are produced globally each year, and at least 8 million tons end up in the ocean annually.
 
• In India, the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** reported that plastic waste generation amounted to **3.5 million tons annually** in 2020.
 
 
 
• **Environmental impact of disposable plastics:**
 
 
• Plastic waste contributes to **soil and water pollution**, as it takes hundreds of years to decompose, releasing harmful chemicals in the process.
 
• Animals often mistake plastic for food, leading to ingestion and severe health issues, and in some cases, fatalities.
 
• Incineration of plastic waste releases **toxic gases**, contributing to air pollution and climate change.
 
 
 
• **Government initiatives to combat plastic waste:**
 
 
• The Indian government launched the **Plastic Waste Management Rules (2016)** to regulate the use and disposal of plastic. In 2022, single-use plastics were banned in India.
 
• The **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (Clean India Mission)** emphasizes waste segregation and recycling, including plastic waste.
 
 
 
• **Alternatives to disposable plastics:**
 
 
• Use of **biodegradable materials** such as jute bags, bamboo straws, and paper-based packaging is gaining popularity.
 
• Encouraging the use of **metal or glass containers** for storage and reusable bottles for water and beverages can significantly reduce plastic waste.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Features of disposable plastics:**

 
 
• They are lightweight, low-cost, and convenient for single-use applications, making them widely used in packaging, food services, and retail.
 
• However, their non-biodegradable nature poses a significant threat to the environment.
 
 
 
• **Impact of bans on plastic waste:**
 
 
• Bans on single-use plastics have been implemented in various countries, including **India**, **Canada**, and the **European Union**, to curb plastic pollution.
 
• While these measures are effective, they require strict enforcement and public cooperation to achieve desired results.

questions.question: When the height of an object is doubled, its potential energy becomes:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**double**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Potential Energy (PE)** is given by the formula: PE = m × g × h, where:

 
 
• **m** is the mass of the object (in kilograms).
 
• **g** is the acceleration due to gravity (approximately 9.8 m/s²).
 
• **h** is the height of the object above a reference point (in meters).
 
 
 
• When the **height (h)** of an object is doubled, the formula becomes: PE = m × g × (2h).
 
• This results in the potential energy becoming 2 × (m × g × h), i.e., **double the original potential energy**.
 
• Hence, the potential energy of the object is directly proportional to its height. Doubling the height leads to a doubling of the potential energy.
 
• Thus, the correct answer is that the potential energy becomes **double**</u&g

questions.question: When calcium oxide reacts with water, the product formed is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**calcium hydroxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When **calcium oxide** (commonly known as quicklime) reacts with water, it forms **calcium hydroxide** (slaked lime) through an exothermic reaction.
 
• The chemical equation for this reaction is:

 **CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + Heat**.
 
• This reaction releases a significant amount of heat, making it an **exothermic reaction**.
 
• The product formed, **calcium hydroxide**, is a white powder or a suspension in water, often used in construction (e.g., making mortar) and as a disinfectant in water treatment.
 
• Other options like **calcium chloride, calcium carbonate,** and **calcium sulphate** are not formed in this reaction. These compounds are the result of entirely different chemical reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Calcium Oxide (Quicklime):**

 
 
• It is a chemical compound with the formula **CaO**.
 
• Quicklime is a white, caustic, alkaline crystalline solid at room temperature.
 
• It is commonly used in the production of cement, steel manufacturing, and as a chemical reagent.
 
 
 
• **Calcium Hydroxide (Slaked Lime):**
 
 
• The chemical formula of calcium hydroxide is **Ca(OH)₂**.
 
• It is widely used in whitewashing, water purification, and as a neutralizing agent in acidic soils.
 
• When dissolved in water, it forms a solution known as lime water, which turns milky in the presence of carbon dioxide.
 
 
 
• **Exothermic Reaction:**
 
 
• Reactions that release heat to the surroundings are termed as **exothermic reactions**.
 
• The reaction between calcium oxide and water is highly exothermic, which can cause boiling and splashing if not handled carefully.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Calcium Chloride:** Formed by the reaction of calcium and hydrochloric acid, not by reacting calcium oxide with water.
 
• **Calcium Carbonate:** Formed when calcium hydroxide reacts with carbon dioxide, resulting in CaCO₃.
 
• **Calcium Sulphate:** Commonly known as gypsum, it is formed by the reaction of calcium compounds with sulphuric acid or sulphates.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The reaction between calcium oxide and water is an industrially significant process in the production of slaked lime, used in various construction and chemical applications.
 
• Lime water (a solution of calcium hydroxide in water) is a popular test for carbon dioxide gas as it turns milky in its presence due to the formation of calcium carbonate.
 
• Calcium hydroxide is used in agriculture to neutralize acidic soils and improve soil fertility.
 
• Safety measures should be taken while handling quicklime as its reaction with water is vigorous and can cause burns.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes the process of budding in organisms like Hydra?

options.text: A bud forms only during sexual reproduction and fuses with the parent organism.
A bud forms as an outgrowth due to repeated cell division and detaches when mature.
A bud forms from specialised cells inside the organism and remains attached for life.
A bud forms from a broken body part and grows into a new organism.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A bud forms as an outgrowth due to repeated cell division and detaches when mature.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Budding** is an asexual reproduction process observed in organisms like **Hydra**, yeast, and some other species.
 
• In this process, a bud forms as an **outgrowth** on the body of the parent organism due to **repeated mitotic cell division.**
 
• The bud remains attached to the parent organism while it grows and matures, drawing nutrients and support from the parent.
 
• Once the bud is fully developed, it **detaches** from the parent and becomes an independent organism capable of surviving on its own.
 
• This process ensures the **continuity of the species** without the need for gamete fusion, as seen in sexual reproduction. **Hydra** is a well-known example of organisms reproducing through budding.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Explanation of Other Options:**

 
 
• **Option 1:** "A bud forms only during sexual reproduction and fuses with the parent organism" – This is **incorrect**. Budding is a form of **asexual reproduction**, and the bud does not fuse with the parent; it detaches to form a new organism.
 
• **Option 3:** "A bud forms from specialized cells inside the organism and remains attached for life" – This is **incorrect**. The bud forms externally and detaches once it matures.
 
• **Option 4:** "A bud forms from a broken body part and grows into a new organism" – This is **incorrect**. This description refers to **regeneration**, not budding. For example, starfish regenerate lost arms, but this is not budding.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Budding:**
 
 
• Budding is common in **Hydra**, **yeast**, and certain plants and fungi.
 
• In **yeast**, the process involves the formation of a small bulge on the parent cell, which grows and eventually separates as a new cell.
 
• In **Hydra**, budding occurs through mitotic cell division in the body wall, forming a miniature version of the parent.
 
• This process is energy-efficient as it does not require the production of gametes or mating.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Asexual Reproduction Methods:**
 
 
• **Fragmentation:** Seen in organisms like **spirogyra**, where the body breaks into fragments, and each fragment grows into a new organism.
 
• **Binary Fission:** Found in bacteria, where the organism divides into two identical daughter cells.
 
• **Sporulation:** Seen in fungi and some plants, where spores develop into new organisms under favorable conditions.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Budding:**
 
 
• Ensures **rapid reproduction** in favorable conditions.
 
• Helps maintain the population of species in stable environments.
 
• Simple and efficient mechanism for producing genetically identical offspring.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hydra:**

 
 
• Hydra is a **freshwater organism** belonging to the phylum **Cnidaria**.
 
• It reproduces both sexually and asexually, with budding being its common mode of asexual reproduction.
 
• Hydra’s ability to regenerate is another significant characteristic, which allows it to recover lost body parts.
 
 
 
• **Yeast:**
 
 
• Yeast is a unicellular fungus that reproduces primarily through budding.
 
• It is used in baking, brewing, and scientific research due to its rapid growth and easy genetic manipulation.
 
• In yeast, a small bud appears, grows, and eventually separates to form an independent organism.

questions.question: An object with a mass of 10.0 { kg} is initially moving at a velocity of 3.0 { m/s} . A constant force of 30.0 { N} is applied in the opposite direction of its motion for 5.0 { s} . What is the final velocity of the object?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**-12.0 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Initial velocity of the object:** The object has an initial velocity of **3.0 m/s** in a specific direction. This is the starting motion of the object. (Correct)
 
• **Mass of the object:** The mass of the object is given as **10.0 kg**. This is used to compute the acceleration when the force is applied. (Correct)
 
• **Force applied:** A constant force of **30.0 N** is applied in the opposite direction of motion. This force will decelerate the object. (Correct)
 
• **Duration of force application:** The force acts on the object for **5.0 seconds**. This time duration is crucial in determining the change in velocity. (Correct)
 
• **Final velocity calculation:** Using Newton's second law and kinematic equations, the final velocity is calculated as **-12.0 m/s**, indicating the object is moving in the opposite direction after deceleration. (Correct)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion:** The law states that the force acting on an object is equal to the product of its mass and acceleration. Formula: **F = ma**. Here, force is **30.0 N**, and mass is **10.0 kg**. This gives an acceleration of **a = F/m = 30/10 = 3.0 m/s²**.
 
• **Acceleration Direction:** Since the force is applied in the opposite direction to motion, the acceleration is **negative**. Thus, **a = -3.0 m/s²**.
 
• **Kinematic Equation:** The final velocity can be calculated using the equation: **v = u + at**, where **v** is the final velocity, **u** is the initial velocity, **a** is the acceleration, and **t** is the time. Substituting the values: **v = 3.0 + (-3.0) * 5.0 = 3.0 - 15.0 = -12.0 m/s**.
 
• **Negative Velocity:** The final velocity being **-12.0 m/s** indicates that the object has reversed its direction and is now moving opposite to its initial motion.
 
• **Applications of the Concept:** This principle is widely used in understanding vehicle braking systems, rocket propulsion, and other real-world scenarios involving motion under opposing forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Force Opposing Motion:** When a force is applied opposite to the direction of motion, it causes deceleration, which is reflected as a negative acceleration in calculations.
 
• **Sign Convention:** In physics problems, the direction of motion is often considered positive, and opposing forces or velocities are assigned negative values.
 
• **Real-Life Example:** A car braking to a stop exemplifies deceleration. If the braking force is strong enough, the car can even reverse its direction, similar to the object in this problem.
 
• **Key Formula:** Always remember the equation **v = u + at** for problems involving uniform acceleration or deceleration.
 
• **Practical Implications:** Understanding motion under opposing forces is crucial in designing safety systems like airbags, seat belts, and crash avoidance technologies.

questions.question: When particles of two different types of matter randomly mix due to the inherent random movement of particles, the process is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**diffusion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Diffusion** is the process by which particles of two different types of matter mix randomly due to their inherent kinetic energy and random motion.
 
• It occurs naturally without the need for external force or pressure, as particles move from regions of higher concentration to regions of lower concentration.
 
• This phenomenon is common in both gases and liquids, where molecules are free to move and spread.
 
• **Examples:** The fragrance of perfume spreading in a room or sugar dissolving in water are examples of diffusion.
 
• Diffusion is crucial in biological processes, such as gas exchange in the lungs (oxygen diffuses into blood, and carbon dioxide diffuses out).

questions.question: Why does carbon form covalent bonds instead of ionic bonds?

options.text: It is energetically unfavourable to lose or gain 4 electrons.
It has a very large atomic radius.
Carbon can easily gain or lose 4 electrons.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is energetically unfavourable to lose or gain 4 electrons.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carbon's electronic configuration**: Carbon has an atomic number of **6**, and its electronic configuration is **1s² 2s² 2p²**. It has **4 valence electrons** in its outermost shell.
 
• **Energetic considerations for ionic bonding**: To form an ionic bond, carbon would need to either **gain 4 electrons** to achieve a stable octet (resulting in a -4 charge) or **lose 4 electrons** (resulting in a +4 charge). Both processes require a **tremendous amount of energy**, making them highly **energetically unfavourable**.
 
• **Covalent bonding as a solution**: Instead of forming ionic bonds, carbon achieves stability by **sharing its 4 electrons** with other atoms through covalent bonds. This sharing allows carbon to complete its octet with minimal energy expenditure.
 
• **Small atomic size**: Carbon's small atomic size makes it suitable for forming stable covalent bonds by overlapping its orbitals with those of other atoms, enabling strong bond formation.
 
• **Versatility of covalent bonding**: Carbon forms covalent bonds with a wide variety of elements, including hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and other carbon atoms. This property allows it to create an extensive range of compounds, including organic molecules essential for life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbon's tetravalency**: Carbon is **tetravalent**, meaning it can form four covalent bonds. This property allows it to create a diverse array of compounds, ranging from simple molecules like methane (CH₄) to complex macromolecules like DNA.
 
• **Allotropes of carbon**: Carbon exists in several allotropes, including **diamond**, **graphite**, and **fullerenes**. These allotropes demonstrate the versatility of carbon's covalent bonding.
 
• **Hybridization in carbon**: Carbon exhibits different types of hybridization (sp, sp², sp³), allowing it to form single, double, and triple bonds. For example, sp³ hybridization occurs in methane, while sp² hybridization is seen in ethene.
 
• **Importance in organic chemistry**: Carbon's ability to form stable covalent bonds is the foundation of organic chemistry, which studies compounds primarily composed of carbon and hydrogen.
 
• **Comparison with other elements**: Unlike elements such as sodium or chlorine, which readily lose or gain one electron to form ionic bonds, carbon's intermediate position in the periodic table makes covalent bonding the most practical and energetically efficient option.

questions.question: In a purely resistive circuit, the electrical energy supplied by the battery is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**completely dissipated as heat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **purely resistive circuit**, the electrical energy supplied by the battery is fully converted into **heat energy**. This is a fundamental property of resistive components, governed by **Joule’s Law of Heating**.
 
• According to **Joule's Law**, the heat energy generated in a resistive element is proportional to the square of the current, the resistance, and the time for which the current flows. The formula is: **H = I²RT**, where H is heat, I is current, R is resistance, and T is time.
 
• Resistors do not store energy in any form. They dissipate energy continuously as **heat** when current flows through them.
 
• Unlike inductors or capacitors, which can store energy as **magnetic** or **electric fields** respectively, resistors solely serve to oppose the flow of current and convert electrical energy into heat.
 
• This phenomenon is utilized in various applications, such as **electric heaters, toasters, and incandescent light bulbs**, where resistive elements are designed to generate heat intentionally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Energy Conversion in Resistive Circuits:**

 
 
• In a resistive circuit, **electrical energy** is transformed directly into **thermal energy** due to the opposition to current flow caused by the resistor.
 
• The power dissipated as heat in the resistor is given by **P = I²R = V²/R**, where P is power, I is current, V is voltage, and R is resistance.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Components:**
 
 
• **Inductors:** Store energy in the form of a **magnetic field**. The energy stored is given by **E = ½LI²**, where L is inductance and I is current.
 
• **Capacitors:** Store energy in the form of an **electric field**. The energy stored is given by **E = ½CV²**, where C is capacitance and V is voltage.
 
• **Resistors:** Do not store energy but dissipate it entirely as heat.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Resistive Heating:**
 
 
• **Electric Heating Devices:** Appliances like **electric heaters, hair dryers, and ovens** use resistive elements to convert electrical energy into heat.
 
• **Incandescent Bulbs:** Filaments in these bulbs are resistive and glow due to the heat generated, producing light.
 
• **Fuses:** Resistive heating is utilized in fuses to break the circuit when excessive current flows.
 
 
 
• **Important Characteristics of a Resistive Circuit:**
 
 
• **Ohmic Behavior:** Resistors obey **Ohm's Law**, where voltage (V) across the resistor is directly proportional to the current (I) flowing through it, i.e., V = IR.
 
• **No Energy Storage:** Unlike capacitors or inductors, resistors do not have the ability to store energy.
 
• **Uniform Dissipation:** The energy is uniformly dissipated as heat along the resistive element.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1:** Stored as magnetic energy – This is incorrect because only **inductors** can store energy as a magnetic field.
 
• **Option 2:** Stored as potential energy – This is incorrect because **capacitors**, not resistors, store energy as potential energy in the form of an electric field.
 
• **Option 3:** Completely dissipated as heat – This is correct as resistors convert all electrical energy into heat.
 
• **Option 4:** Converted only into light – This is incorrect. While resistors in devices like incandescent bulbs emit light, it is a by-product of the heat generated.

questions.question: Which of the following is essential for the propagation of sound waves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Medium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sound waves require a medium for propagation**, as they travel by causing vibrations in the particles of a material medium such as solids, liquids, or gases.
 
• In a **solid medium**, particles are closely packed, allowing sound to travel faster compared to liquids and gases.
 
• Sound cannot travel through a **vacuum**, as there are no particles present to vibrate and transfer the sound energy. *(This makes Option 3 incorrect).*
 
• Unlike light waves, which can travel through a vacuum, sound waves are **mechanical waves** and depend on the interaction of particles in a medium. *(This excludes Options 1, 2).*
 
• The **speed of sound** varies depending on the medium. For example, sound travels at approximately 343 m/s in air, 1,480 m/s in water, and up to 5,000 m/s in steel.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Sound Waves:**

 
 
• Sound waves are **longitudinal waves**, meaning the particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
 
• They are also **mechanical waves**, requiring a medium such as air, water, or solids to transmit energy.
 
• Sound waves consist of compressions (regions of high pressure) and rarefactions (regions of low pressure).
 
 
 
• **Role of Medium:**
 
 
• The type of medium affects the **speed, intensity, and quality** of sound.
 
• Sound travels fastest in **solids**, slower in **liquids**, and slowest in **gases**, due to the density and elasticity of the medium.
 
• For example, sound travels faster in water (1,480 m/s) than in air (343 m/s).
 
 
 
• **Sound in a Vacuum:**
 
 
• In a vacuum, there are no particles to vibrate and carry sound waves, so sound cannot propagate.
 
• This principle is why astronauts in space require radio communication, as space is essentially a vacuum.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Sound Propagation:**
 
 
• In air: Sound from a speaker or a person talking travels through the air to reach your ears.
 
• In water: Marine animals like dolphins use sound to communicate over long distances underwater.
 
• In solids: Vibrations from a tuning fork can be felt through a table or metal rod.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1: Magnet** - A magnet is unrelated to sound propagation, as it affects magnetic fields, not mechanical waves.
 
• **Option 2: Light Source** - A light source emits electromagnetic waves, which can travel through a vacuum, unlike sound waves.
 
• **Option 3: Vacuum** - A vacuum lacks particles, making it impossible for sound to propagate through it.
 
• **Option 4: Medium** - A medium (solid, liquid, or gas) is essential for the propagation of sound waves, as it provides the particles needed for the transfer of energy.
 
• **Option 5: None** - This is incorrect, as a medium is mandatory for sound to travel.

questions.question: The mode of cell division by which germ cells get half the amount of DNA as compared to non-reproductive cells is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meiosis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meiosis** is a type of cell division that occurs in germ cells (reproductive cells).
 
• It reduces the chromosome number by half, producing four haploid cells (gametes) from a single diploid parent cell.
 
• This process ensures that the offspring have the same chromosome number as the parent organism when gametes fuse during fertilization.
 
• **Meiosis** consists of two sequential stages: *Meiosis I* and *Meiosis II*, each with specific phases like prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase.
 
• During **Meiosis I**, homologous chromosomes separate, and during **Meiosis II**, sister chromatids separate, resulting in the formation of four genetically distinct gametes.
 
• This process is crucial for maintaining genetic diversity through mechanisms like crossing over and independent assortment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Budding**:

 
 
• This is an asexual form of reproduction seen in organisms like yeast and hydra.
 
• A new individual develops as an outgrowth (bud) on the parent organism and eventually detaches to live independently.
 
• It does not involve the reduction of chromosome number or the formation of gametes.
 
 
 
• **Mitosis**:
 
 
• Mitosis is a type of cell division in which a single parent cell divides to produce two genetically identical daughter cells.
 
• It occurs in somatic (non-reproductive) cells and is responsible for growth, tissue repair, and asexual reproduction.
 
• Unlike meiosis, mitosis maintains the original chromosome number (diploid) in daughter cells.
 
 
 
• **Amitosis**:
 
 
• Amitosis is a direct type of cell division without the formation of spindle fibers or distinct chromosomes.
 
• It occurs in some unicellular organisms like bacteria and certain protozoa.
 
• This process is much simpler and lacks the complexity of meiosis or mitosis.
 
 
 
• **Role of Meiosis in Genetic Diversity:**
 
 
• Genetic recombination occurs during **crossing over** in Prophase I of Meiosis I, which exchanges genetic material between homologous chromosomes.
 
• **Independent assortment** of chromosomes during Metaphase I leads to a variety of genetic combinations.
 
• These mechanisms contribute to evolutionary processes by introducing variability in populations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Meiosis and Fertilization:**

 
 
• Meiosis ensures that gametes (sperm and egg) have half the chromosome number (haploid).
 
• Fertilization restores the diploid chromosome number in the zygote, ensuring species consistency.
 
 
 
• **Organisms Exhibiting Meiosis:**
 
 
• Meiosis occurs in sexually reproducing organisms, including animals, plants, and fungi.
 
• In plants, meiosis leads to the formation of spores, which eventually develop into gametophytes.
 
 
 
• **Medical Relevance:**
 
 
• Errors in meiosis can lead to chromosomal abnormalities such as **Down syndrome, Klinefelter syndrome,** or **Turner syndrome**.
 
• Understanding meiosis is crucial for fertility treatments and genetic counseling.

questions.question: When light ray passes from a rarer medium to a denser medium, it ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**bends towards the normal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a light ray passes from a **rarer medium** (like air) to a **denser medium** (like water or glass), it **bends towards the normal**. This phenomenon occurs due to the change in the speed of light as it moves between media of different optical densities.
 
• The bending of light at the interface of two media is governed by **Snell's Law**, which states that the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is constant for a given pair of media.
 
• The refractive index of the denser medium is **greater** than that of the rarer medium, causing the light ray to slow down and bend towards the normal.
 
• The angle of refraction is always **smaller** than the angle of incidence when light travels from a rarer to a denser medium.
 
• Examples of this phenomenon include the bending of light when it passes from air into water, making objects submerged in water appear displaced or distorted.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Snell's Law:**

 
 
• Snell's Law is mathematically expressed as: **n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂**, where **n₁** and **n₂** are the refractive indices of the two media, and θ₁ and θ₂ are the angles of incidence and refraction, respectively.
 
• It explains the relationship between the angles and the refractive indices of the two media.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index:**
 
 
• The refractive index is a measure of how much the speed of light is reduced inside a medium compared to its speed in a vacuum.
 
• For example, the refractive index of air is approximately 1.0003, while that of water is about 1.33, and glass ranges from 1.5 to 1.9.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Refraction:**
 
 
• Refraction is utilized in the design of optical instruments such as **lenses, microscopes, and telescopes**.
 
• It is also responsible for natural phenomena like the formation of rainbows and the apparent bending of objects in water.
 
 
 
• **Critical Angle and Total Internal Reflection:**
 
 
• When light travels from a denser medium to a rarer medium, at a certain angle called the **critical angle**, the refracted ray travels along the boundary.
 
• If the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle, the light undergoes **total internal reflection**, a principle used in optical fibers and periscopes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 2 (bends at a 90° angle):** This is incorrect because light does not bend at a 90° angle unless it is incident at the critical angle and refracts along the boundary.
 
• **Option 3 (bends away from the normal):** This occurs when light travels from a denser medium to a rarer medium, not the other way around.
 
• **Option 4 (does not bend at all):** This is true only if the light ray is incident normally (perpendicular) to the surface, in which case it passes straight through without refraction.
 
• Understanding the concept of refraction is crucial in fields like **optics, physics, and engineering**, where precision in light manipulation is required.

questions.question: What does the atomic number of an element represent?

options.text: Number of neurons in an atom
Total number of electrons and protons
Number of protons in an atom

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Number of protons in an atom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **atomic number** of an element represents the **number of protons** present in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• The atomic number is a unique identifier for each element in the **periodic table**, meaning no two elements share the same atomic number.
 
• The number of protons in an atom determines its **chemical properties** and its position in the periodic table.
 
• For a neutral atom, the number of protons is equal to the number of **electrons**, ensuring electrical neutrality.
 
• The atomic number is denoted by the symbol **Z** in nuclear and atomic physics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1: Number of Neutrons in an Atom**

 
 
• The **number of neutrons** in an atom is not represented by its atomic number. Instead, neutrons are calculated by subtracting the atomic number from the **mass number** (Mass Number = Protons + Neutrons).
 
• The number of neutrons can vary among isotopes of the same element, leading to different atomic masses.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Mass Number of the Atom**
 
 
• The **mass number** is the sum of protons and neutrons in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• Unlike the atomic number, the mass number is not unique to an element because it can vary for isotopes of the same element.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Total Number of Electrons and Protons**
 
 
• The atomic number does not represent the combined total of electrons and protons. However, in a **neutral atom**, the number of electrons is equal to the number of protons.
 
• In ions, the number of electrons differs from the number of protons due to gain or loss of electrons.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Number of Protons in an Atom**
 
 
• This is the **correct answer** as the atomic number directly corresponds to the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• For example, the element **Hydrogen** has an atomic number of 1, meaning it has 1 proton, while **Carbon** has an atomic number of 6, meaning it has 6 protons.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Atomic Number**
 
 
• The atomic number determines the element's **identity** and its position in the periodic table.
 
• It is crucial in defining the element's **chemical behavior** and reactivity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Periodic Table**: The periodic table is organized based on the atomic number of elements, with elements arranged in increasing order of atomic number.
 
• **Isotopes**: Atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers are called isotopes. For example, **Carbon-12** and **Carbon-14** are isotopes of Carbon.
 
• **Discovery**: The concept of the atomic number was proposed by **Henry Moseley** in 1913 through his work on X-ray spectra.
 
• **Neutral Atoms**: In a neutral atom, the atomic number also indicates the number of **electrons**, which balance the positive charge of the protons.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements and select the correct option.

Statement 1: A fuse is connected in series in an electric circuit.

Statement 2: A fuse wire melts when the current exceeds a safe limit.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both Statements 1 and 2 are correct.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** A fuse is connected in series in an electric circuit.

 
 
• A **fuse** is always connected in **series** with the electrical circuit it protects.
 
• This ensures that the fuse can effectively interrupt the flow of current to the entire circuit when there is an overload or short circuit.
 
• By being in series, any excessive current passes through the fuse first, protecting the devices downstream. ***Hence, Statement 1 is correct.***
 
 
 
• **Statement 2:** A fuse wire melts when the current exceeds a safe limit.
 
 
• A fuse is designed with a wire of low melting point and specific current-carrying capacity.
 
• When the current in the circuit exceeds the safe limit, the heat generated by the excess current causes the fuse wire to melt.
 
• This action breaks the circuit and prevents damage to electrical appliances and fires caused by overheating. ***Hence, Statement 2 is correct.***
 
 
 
• Both statements are **true** as they describe the purpose and working principle of a fuse in an electric circuit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fuse:**

 
 
• A **fuse** is a safety device used in electrical circuits to protect appliances from overloads and short circuits.
 
• It is made of a metal or alloy with a low melting point and high conductivity, typically **tin-lead alloy** or **copper**.
 
 
 
• **Functions of a Fuse:**
 
 
• It protects electrical devices by interrupting excessive current flow.
 
• Prevents overheating and potential fire hazards in the circuit.
 
• Ensures the safety of users by disconnecting the faulty circuit.
 
 
 
• **Types of Fuses:**
 
 
• **Cartridge Fuse:** Used in appliances and automotive circuits.
 
• **Rewireable Fuse:** Common in domestic wiring systems.
 
• **Miniature Circuit Breaker (MCB):** Modern alternative to traditional fuses, automatically trips during faults.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Fuses:**
 
 
• Used in **domestic wiring** systems to protect home appliances.
 
• Widely utilized in **industrial machinery** to prevent electrical hazards.
 
• Essential in **automotive circuits** to safeguard vehicle electronics.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Melting Point of Fuse Wire:**

 
 
• The fuse wire is selected based on its **low melting point** so that it melts quickly during excessive current flow.
 
 
 
• **Proper Rating:**
 
 
• Fuses must have the correct **current rating** to provide effective protection; an undersized fuse may blow unnecessarily, while an oversized fuse may fail to protect the circuit.
 
 
 
• **Maintenance:**
 
 
• Regular inspection of fuse connections is necessary to ensure they are functioning properly and are not damaged.

questions.question: The molecular mass of HNO₃ is 63 atomic mass unit (u). What is atomic mass of oxygen (O)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**16u**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The molecular mass of HNO₃**: The molecular mass of nitric acid (HNO₃) is given as **63u**, where "u" represents atomic mass units.
 
• **Composition of HNO₃**: Nitric acid is composed of **1 hydrogen atom (H)**, **1 nitrogen atom (N)**, and **3 oxygen atoms (O)**.
 
• **Atomic masses of hydrogen and nitrogen**: The atomic mass of hydrogen (H) is **1u**, and the atomic mass of nitrogen (N) is **14u**.
 
• **Mass contribution of oxygen**: The total molecular mass of HNO₃ is calculated as follows:

 **Molecular mass = Mass of H + Mass of N + (3 × Mass of O)**

 Substituting the values: **63 = 1 + 14 + (3 × Mass of O)**.
 
• **Solving for oxygen's atomic mass**: Simplifying the equation:

 **63 = 15 + 3 × Mass of O**

 **48 = 3 × Mass of O**

 **Mass of O = 48 ÷ 3 = 16u**.
 
• **Conclusion**: The atomic mass of oxygen is **16u**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atomic Mass Unit (u):**

 
 
• An atomic mass unit (u) is a standard unit of mass that quantifies the mass of an atom or molecule. It is equivalent to **1/12th the mass of a carbon-12 atom**.
 
• The atomic masses of elements are expressed in "u" and are based on their isotopic abundances.
 
 
 
• **Atomic Mass of Common Elements:**
 
 
• **Hydrogen (H):** 1u.
 
• **Carbon (C):** 12u.
 
• **Nitrogen (N):** 14u.
 
• **Oxygen (O):** 16u.
 
 
 
• **Molecular Mass:**
 
 
• The molecular mass of a compound is the sum of the atomic masses of all atoms in its molecular formula.
 
• For example, the molecular mass of water (H₂O) is calculated as:

 **Molecular mass = (2 × Mass of H) + (1 × Mass of O) = (2 × 1u) + (1 × 16u) = 18u.**
 
 
 
• **Applications of Atomic and Molecular Mass:**
 
 
• Used in **stoichiometric calculations** to determine the proportions of reactants and products in chemical reactions.
 
• Helps in calculating **molar masses**, which are crucial for laboratory preparations and industrial processes.
 
• Essential for understanding molecular structures and their behavior in different states of matter.
 
 
 
• **Oxygen in Nature:**
 
 
• Oxygen is a vital element, making up approximately **21% of Earth's atmosphere**.
 
• It is essential for **respiration** in living organisms and is a key component of water (H₂O).
 
• Oxygen is also involved in combustion and various industrial processes, such as steelmaking.

questions.question: Which metal is placed just above copper in the reactivity series?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lead**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **reactivity series** is a list of metals arranged in order of their reactivity from most reactive to least reactive. It is a fundamental concept in chemistry used to predict the behavior of metals in reactions.
 
• **Lead** is placed just above **Copper** in the reactivity series. This is because lead is slightly more reactive than copper but less reactive than metals like iron, zinc, or aluminum.
 
• The placement of lead above copper in the reactivity series means that lead can displace copper from its compounds in certain chemical reactions, such as in displacement reactions.
 
• Copper, being lower in the series, is less reactive and does not displace hydrogen from acids or react with water under normal conditions. Lead, however, can react with certain acids, although it reacts more slowly compared to more reactive metals like zinc or aluminum.
 
• The reactivity series is critical in understanding metal extraction and corrosion. For example, lead is used in applications like batteries because of its moderate reactivity and resistance to corrosion, whereas copper is widely used in electrical wiring due to its low reactivity and excellent conductivity.

questions.question: Which part in the neuron i.e. nervous tissue is responsible for protein synthesis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nissl granules**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Nissl granules** are specialized structures found in the cytoplasm of neurons, particularly in the soma (cell body) and dendrites.
 
• These granules are composed of **rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) and ribosomes**, which are crucial for protein synthesis.
 
• Neurons require extensive protein synthesis to produce neurotransmitters, enzymes, and structural proteins essential for maintaining their function and communication.
 
• Proteins synthesized by Nissl granules are transported throughout the neuron, including the axon and dendrites, to support cellular activities.
 
• Nissl granules are absent in the axon and axon hillock, which is why protein synthesis predominantly occurs in the soma and dendrites.
 
• **Hence, Nissl granules are vital for maintaining the structural and functional integrity of neurons.**
